categories.title: Arrest & Police Custody Rights
categories.summary: Constitutional safeguards when interrogated, detained, or arrested by police officers in India.

items.right: Right to Know Grounds of Arrest & Warrant Inspection
items.simpleExplanation: The police cannot simply detain you without showing a warrant (for non-cognizable cases) or explicitly declaring what offence you are suspected of.
items.legalSource: Article 22(1) of Constitution of India & Section 47 of BNSS, 2023 (Section 50 CrPC)
whatYouCanDo: Politely request to inspect the warrant or ask for the specific section of law.
Ask whether the offence alleged is bailable or non-bailable.
Do not resist physically, but note badge numbers and names.

items.right: Right to Inform a Relative or Friend Immediately
items.simpleExplanation: Police are under strict statutory duty to inform a designated relative or friend about your arrest and the exact station where you are held.
items.legalSource: Section 48 of BNSS, 2023 & D.K. Basu v. State of West Bengal (1997)
whatYouCanDo: Provide the police officer with your nominated family member's phone number.
Ensure the time of informing is noted in the station diary (GD).

items.simpleExplanation: No police officer can keep you in police station lock-up beyond 24 hours excluding reasonable travel time without express magistrate orders.
items.legalSource: Article 22(2) of Constitution & Section 58 of BNSS, 2023
whatYouCanDo: Note the exact timestamp when you were brought to the police station.
Inform the magistrate directly if you were detained for more than 24 hours.

items.simpleExplanation: A registered medical practitioner must conduct a complete medical examination of the arrested person immediately after arrest to record physical condition and any pre-existing injuries.
whatYouCanDo: Request medical examination if experiencing any injury or illness.
Ensure any physical marks or torture signs are recorded in the medical memo.

categories.title: Tenant & Landlord Rights
categories.summary: Protections governing security deposits, unlawful evictions, and maintenance duties.

items.simpleExplanation: A landlord cannot arbitrarily withhold or deduct money from your security deposit for normal wear and tear without giving an itemized breakdown.
items.legalSource: Model Tenancy Act, 2021 & State Rent Control Acts
whatYouCanDo: Conduct a video walkthrough of the property at handover.
Issue a formal written notice claiming the deposit with a 15-day timeline.
Approach the Rent Authority or Consumer Commission if withheld unlawfully.

items.right: Protection from Forceful Eviction & Utility Disconnection
items.simpleExplanation: Landlords are prohibited by law from cutting electricity, water, or locking doors without a court order, even if rent is delayed.
items.legalSource: Section 20 of Model Tenancy Act & State Rent Control Legislations
whatYouCanDo: File a complaint immediately with the local police station for wrongful restraint.
File an urgent petition before the Rent Court to restore essential services.

categories.title: Women Safety & Legal Protections
categories.summary: Statutory shields for women including arrest guidelines, workplace sexual harassment, and domestic violence.

items.right: No Arrest of Women Between Sunset and Sunrise
items.simpleExplanation: As a rule, no woman can be arrested after sunset and before sunrise except in extraordinary circumstances with written judicial magistrate permission.
whatYouCanDo: Refuse arrest by male officers after sunset unless a female officer is present with a Judicial Magistrate order.
Call 1091 or 112 if forced by police after dusk.

items.simpleExplanation: Every workplace with 10 or more employees must maintain an Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) to investigate grievances confidentially within 90 days.
items.legalSource: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
whatYouCanDo: Submit a written complaint to the Internal Committee within 3 months of the incident.
Request interim relief such as transfer or paid leave during the inquiry.

categories.title: Consumer Rights & Fair Trade
categories.summary: Protections against counterfeit goods, defective services, misleading ads, and unfair contract terms.

items.right: Right to Replacement or Full Refund for Defective Products
items.simpleExplanation: Sellers and e-commerce platforms cannot disclaim liability with 'No return under any circumstances' if a good is defective or counterfeit.
items.legalSource: Section 2(47) & Section 84 of Consumer Protection Act, 2019
whatYouCanDo: Preserve purchase invoices, unboxing video clips, and merchant communication.
Lodge a grievance on the National Consumer Helpline (1915).
File an online complaint on e-Daakhil (edaakhil.nic.in).

categories.title: Traffic Police & Challan Protocol
categories.summary: Rules governing vehicle stops, breathalyzers, document verification, and electronic receipts.

items.right: Digital Driving License & RC Validity via DigiLocker
items.simpleExplanation: Traffic police must accept electronic Driving License, RC, and Insurance shown on DigiLocker or mParivahan; physical originals are not mandatory.
items.legalSource: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Notification RT-11036/64/2017-MVL
whatYouCanDo: Present documents in the official DigiLocker app directly.
Do not surrender your phone; simply show the verified barcode/document.

items.right: Traffic Police Cannot Snatch Ignition Keys
items.simpleExplanation: Traffic personnel are strictly prohibited by police manuals from forcibly removing ignition keys from moving or stopped vehicles.
items.legalSource: Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 & State Police Circulars
whatYouCanDo: Turn off the engine calmly and step out if requested.
Politely request the officer's name, e-challan machine ID, or bodycam footage.

categories.title: Right to Information (RTI)
categories.summary: Statutory right to access government records, public works inspection, and administrative documents.

items.simpleExplanation: Any Indian citizen can file an RTI request with a 10 rupee fee, and the Public Information Officer (PIO) must furnish information within 30 days (or 48 hours for life & liberty).
items.legalSource: Section 7(1) of Right to Information Act, 2005
whatYouCanDo: File an online RTI via rtionline.gov.in.
File a First Appeal if no response is received after 30 days.

categories.title: Senior Citizens' Protections
categories.summary: Rights of elderly parents to maintenance, welfare tribunals, and revocation of gifted property.

items.right: Right to Monthly Maintenance from Adult Children
items.simpleExplanation: Senior citizens unable to maintain themselves can approach the Maintenance Tribunal for an order directing children or legal heirs to provide monthly sustenance.
items.legalSource: Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007
whatYouCanDo: File an application before the Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) / Maintenance Tribunal.
Proceedings are summary and do not require expensive advocate fees.

categories.title: Digital Privacy & Data Protection
categories.summary: Rights regarding personal data collection, consent withdrawal, and grievance redressal against data fiduciaries.

items.right: Right to Withdraw Consent and Erasure of Personal Data
items.simpleExplanation: Digital companies cannot retain your personal information indefinitely once the specified service purpose is completed or consent is revoked.
items.legalSource: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (DPDP Act)
whatYouCanDo: Send a data erasure or consent withdrawal request to the company's Data Protection Officer.
Escalate to the Data Protection Board of India if unaddressed.
